# kiss-ssg

> A small, dependency-driven static site generator for Node. MVC-style: Handlebars views, JSON/HTTP/function models, JS controllers. ESM package (Node ≥22.12); engine in `lib/`, entry `lib/kiss.js`. No build step, no bundler.

Install: `npm install kiss-ssg --save-dev`. `import Kiss from 'kiss-ssg'` (CJS `require('kiss-ssg')` also works on Node ≥22.12). Everything is driven by a `Kiss` instance built with `new Kiss(config)` and used via a chainable API. Pages are queued (not rendered) by `.page()`/`.pages()`/`.scan()`; `.generate()` renders and writes them; `.sitemap()`/`.watch()` are opt-in extras. `config` and its resolved values are available in every view as `this.config`.

## API

- `.page(options)` — register one page. `options.view` (required): a `.hbs` filename relative to `config.folders.pages`, or a template string. `options.model`: a `.json` filename (relative to `config.folders.models`), an `http(s)://` URL (a response with a non-2xx status fails that page — an error body is never used as the model), a plain object, or a folder name (loads every `*.json` in it as an array). `options.controller`: a function `({model}) => optionsPatch`, or a `.js` filename relative to `config.folders.controllers`, run after the model resolves — commonly used to reshape/sort the model or derive `slug`. A controller that throws, a filename that does not exist, or a file that does not export a function fails that page and makes `complete()` reject. `options.title`, `options.description`, `options.path`, `options.slug`, `options.ext` (default `html`; a leading `.` is stripped and the rest slugified, so an `ext` derived from model data cannot steer the output path — `'.xml'` → `xml`, `'../x'` → `x`). `options.config`: per-page config overrides, merged over the global `config` for that page only. Every page renders with its own shallow copy of the resolved config, so a controller mutating `options.config` changes that page alone — not the other pages, the instance's `config`, or the sitemap (nested objects such as `folders` are shared, and the engine never mutates them). `slug`/`path` are inferred from `view`'s file path if omitted — but only when `view` is a `.hbs` filename; a template string gets a random `snippet-N` slug and no path, since its own markup is not a file path. Slugs (and each `path` segment) are normalised by `utils.toSlug`: accented Latin is transliterated (`'Über uns'` → `uber-uns`), everything else outside `a-z0-9` becomes `-`, leading/trailing dashes are trimmed, and a title in a script with no Latin mapping (CJK, Hangul, Cyrillic) falls back to a short stable hash (`p-9736ca69`) so such pages stay distinct instead of all claiming one file. Two pages that resolve to the same output path **fail the build** (`complete()` rejects, naming the path) — only one of them would ever exist on disk.
- `.pages(options)` — same as `.page()`, but `options.model` must resolve to an array (or a models folder), and it fans out one page per item, appending `-N` to the slug per item unless the controller sets an explicit `slug`.
- `.scan()` — auto-discovers every `.hbs` under `config.folders.pages` you have not already registered (by `view`, so a `.page()` earlier in the same chain wins and the view is not built twice), and calls `.page()` on each with default options. The simplest way to build a whole site: `kiss.scan().generate()`. Under `.watch()` the scan is repeated on every whole-site rebuild, so page files you add or delete while the dev server runs are picked up.
- `.generate(callback)` — waits for every queued page's model to resolve, then renders and writes each page exactly once (HTML minified via `html-minifier-terser`, CSS/JS minified outside dev mode). `callback(data)` fires after every page has been attempted — including any that failed to render or write; page failures don't surface here, they surface via `complete()`. An error thrown by the callback itself (or a rejection from a promise it returns) is a build failure of its own, recorded as `<generate callback>` and reported by `complete()`. Chainable — returns the `Kiss` instance. To await the whole build use `await kiss.complete()`.
- `.complete(callback)` — resolves after every queued page and any `sitemap()` call has finished writing; resolves with the same `data` array `generate` receives. "Every queued page" includes pages queued from a `generate` callback, whether the callback queues them synchronously or after an `await` (the promise an `async` callback returns is part of what `complete()` waits for), and it includes any page queued after the last `generate()` call: `complete()` renders whatever no `generate()` pass reached, so a page whose model resolved late — or one a callback's `scan()` discovered — is never silently dropped from a build that reports success. It renders nothing if you never called `generate()` at all. Work a _synchronous_ callback defers to a later tick (a `setTimeout`-ed `.page()`) is still outside the build — queue pages synchronously, or from an `async` callback. Rejects with an `AggregateError` — `err.failures` = `[{ view, buildTo, error }]`, message `"N page(s) failed to build: <buildTo paths>"` (build paths, not views, since `.pages()` fan-out gives failed entries the same view; entries with no output path, such as a failing controller or callback, are named by `view` instead) — if any page failed to render or write, any controller failed, or a `generate`/`sitemap` callback threw; other pages still build, and the `generate` callback still fires. It rejects **once per build**: a second `complete()` in the same build resolves instead of rejecting again, so the pattern of calling `complete()` from inside a `generate` callback cannot leave a second, unhandled rejection behind. A failed build never runs `complete()`'s own callback. A model failure is not a build failure: it is logged and skipped, and shows up in the resolved data as `{ id, data: null, error }`. A `.hbs` view whose file cannot be read (missing or misspelled) **is** a build failure: that page fails and `complete()` rejects, rather than the filename being written into the output.
- `.sitemap(options, callback)` — writes `sitemap.xml` to `config.folders.build`, derived from every registered page. Requires `config.siteUrl` (logs an error and skips, does not throw, if unset). Can be called before or after `.generate()` — both just wait on the same internal promise queue. Per-page opt-out: `ignoreSitemap: true` in that page's `.page()`/`.pages()` options. Per-page overrides: `sitemapPriority` (default `'1.00'`), `sitemapChangefreq` (omitted from the XML unless set), `sitemapLastmod` (default: one timestamp shared by all pages, captured when `.sitemap()` runs). `options.overwrite` (default `true`) — set `false` to skip (re)writing if `sitemap.xml` already exists; only has an effect if `cleanBuild: false` too, since the default `cleanBuild: true` already empties the whole build dir — including any prior `sitemap.xml` — before `.sitemap()` ever runs.
- `.watch(options)` — starts a `chokidar` watcher on `config.folders.src` (only meaningful with `dev: true`, which also starts a livereload dev server on `config.port`, default `3001`, bound to `config.devHost`, with live reload on `config.livereloadPort`); rebuilds just the affected page(s), or the whole site if a changed file can't be matched to a queued page. Editing a partial or a layout re-registers the partials and re-renders every page, without re-resolving any model (URL models included) or re-running any controller — a partial edit cannot change the page set, a page's options, its output path or the sitemap. Every other non-page change is a whole-site rebuild. A whole-site rebuild replays every `.page()`/`.pages()`/`.scan()` registration from scratch, so edited models and controllers take effect (controller files are reloaded from disk, ESM and CommonJS alike); a single-page rebuild is a template re-render. A whole-site rebuild also deletes output files the previous build wrote that the new one no longer produces (a removed fan-out model, a changed slug, or a page `.scan()` had discovered whose `.hbs` file you deleted — a page you registered by name instead keeps failing the build until you remove the call) and re-runs `.sitemap()` if you ever called it. Creating a file under `src/` rebuilds the whole site too, so a partial or layout you add mid-session is registered and usable straight away, and a new page `.hbs` is built as well if you used `.scan()` (a rebuild scans the pages folder again; on an explicitly registered site you still add the `.page()` call yourself). Deleting a partial or layout unregisters it, so any page still referencing it fails the rebuild with `The partial <name> could not be found` instead of quietly rendering the deleted content until you restart. `options.entry` (default `process.argv[1]`): the script whose change triggers a full rebuild.
- `.close()` — stops the file watcher and dev server (dev mode / after `.watch()`); returns a Promise that resolves once any in-flight rebuild has finished, so nothing is written after it.
- `.copyAssets(sourceDir, targetDir)` — compiles every `*.scss`/`*.sass` under `sourceDir` to a sibling `.css` and copies everything else straight through to `targetDir`. Runs automatically once at construction time for `config.folders.assets` → `config.folders.build`; callable again for extra asset directories. Calls run one after another in registration order, not concurrently.
- `.registerPartials()` — re-registers every partial and layout from disk (`folders.partials`, `folders.layouts`, plus `.md`/`.html` partials), unregistering any name whose file has since gone; returns the list of registered names. Runs automatically at construction and on every watch rebuild — call it yourself to pick up partials added or removed at runtime outside `.watch()`.
- `.viewStats()` — logs the queued-promise and prepared-page counts, and (with `verbose: true`) writes `debug.json` — one entry per page, `{ view, buildTo, runCount, options }` — into `config.folders.build`. Chainable; use it from a `generate` callback to see what a build actually produced.
- `.getModelByID(id, data)` — looks an entry up by `id` in the `[{ id, data }]` array `generate`/`complete` hand back, and returns its `.data` (or `{ error }` if there is no such id). The `id` is the model filename or URL you passed; object models get a hash instead. Use it to pull one page's resolved model out of the build data.
- `kiss.handlebars` — this instance's own Handlebars environment (`Handlebars.create()`, created per `Kiss`, so helpers and partials never leak between instances, and helpers registered on the global `handlebars` module are not seen); register custom helpers on it directly. Built-in helpers: `markdown`, `sass` (inline block or file path — an absolute path is used as given, a relative one resolves against the process working directory; via the modern `sass.compile`/`compileString` API), `offset`, `stringify`, `isActive` (nav active state: the block's `href` is compared to the page URL by whole path segments, with `/about`, `/about/` and the extension-less form all one page, so the same `href` works under either `extensionLess` setting; `folderMatch=true` also matches pages below the href, and an empty `href` then means the home page only), `env` (`{{#env is="dev"}}`/`"prod"` blocks).
- `kiss.remarkable` — this instance's own Markdown renderer (used for `.md` partials and the `markdown` helper).
- `import { utils } from 'kiss-ssg'` — `toSlug`, `sanitizePath`, `toTitleCase`, `trimLines`, `trimPath`, `posixPath`, `globFiles(dir, pattern)`, `hashId`.

## Config

Passed to `new Kiss(config)`. Defaults:

```js
{
  dev: false,          // starts a livereload dev server + file watcher; skips minification
  verbose: false,
  cleanBuild: true,     // empties config.folders.build before generating
  extensionLess: false, // true: non-index pages build to <path>/<slug>/index.html instead of <path>/<slug>.html
  siteUrl: undefined,   // required by .sitemap()
  sass: { includePaths: [] },
  port: 3001,           // dev server port
  livereloadPort: 35729, // live reload port; also the port injected into the dev-mode reload <script>
  devHost: '127.0.0.1',  // interface the dev + live reload servers bind to
  folders: {
    root: './',
    src: './src',
    pages: './src/pages',
    build: './public',
    assets: './src/assets',
    static: './src/static',
    layouts: './src/layouts',
    partials: './src/partials',
    models: './src/models',
    controllers: './src/controllers',
  },
}
```

`livereloadPort` lets two sites run side by side: give the second one its own value, or its pages would poll the first site's live reload server. A clash on the live reload port is logged and live reload is switched off for that site — the dev server keeps serving. `devHost` binds the dev and live reload servers to loopback only; set it to `'0.0.0.0'` to open the preview to other devices on your network.

Setting `folders.src` re-derives every other `folders.*` entry from it, unless that entry is also set explicitly. Folder strings are normalised on the way in — a trailing slash or a backslash separator is tolerated (`'./src/assets/'` and `'.\\src\\assets'` both resolve to `'./src/assets'`).

## Docs

- [README.md](README.md): full usage docs, worked examples for `.page()`/`.pages()`/`.sitemap()`, the helpers list.
- [examples/](examples/): 6 runnable, self-contained demos (`node examples/<N>-name.js`, or `npm run eg<N>`) — scan, page+controller, dynamic pages from a fetched model, layouts/partials, custom helpers, sitemap.
- [lib/](lib/): the engine — `kiss.js` (orchestrator, public API), `kiss-page.js` (one page's render), and one module per concern (`config`, `logger`, `handlebars-helpers`, `partials`, `assets`, `model-resolver`, `controller-resolver`, `sitemap`, `dev-server`, `watcher`, `utils`). Per-module notes: [AIKB/](AIKB/).

## Migrating from v1

- ESM-only (`import Kiss from 'kiss-ssg'`); CJS `require()` still works on Node ≥22.12.
- The `generate` callback now fires after files are written, not before.
- v1 logged a page's render/write failure and resolved anyway; v2's `complete()` rejects with an `AggregateError` listing the failed views.
- Handlebars is per-instance — register helpers on `kiss.handlebars`, not the global `handlebars` module. Partials are registered there too, so a helper reading the global `handlebars.partials` renders nothing; use `kiss.handlebars.partials` or the native dynamic partial `{{> (lookup this "name")}}`.
- `utils` is a named export (`import { utils } from 'kiss-ssg'`), not `kiss-ssg/libs/utils.js`.
- Controllers may `export default` instead of `module.exports =`.
- Duplicate output paths, including `.pages()` fan-out where a controller yields the same slug twice, are no longer written twice: the second page is not built and the collision is a build failure, so `complete()` rejects naming the path (v1 wrote whichever page came last).
